rationale:
RFC_032 was ruled by the owner on 2026-08-22: converge the estate on {{.InstanceID}} and retire {{.ComponentID}}, rather than re-pointing ComponentID. This submission is the FIRST step of that ruling and it is deliberately the smallest one: it makes the ruled remedy EXECUTABLE. It does not convert any template, does not touch any render path, and changes no live behaviour by itself.

The defect being fixed is in the converter itself. ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope harvests declared ids with `\sid="([^"{}]+)"`. The character class excludes braces, so an id written as `id="{{.ComponentID}}"` never enters the declared-id set; with the set empty the function takes the len(seen)==0 branch and refuses with "template declares no literal element ids — nothing to namespace". That reason is the exact opposite of the truth on a template that plainly declares an id. Five active templates are in that state as of 2026-08-22 (generic-text-block, faq, mechanism-flow, evidence-timeseries, pricing), so filing them through the proven conversion pipeline against today's binary would produce five polite no-op completions, a queue that drains clean, and a census that never moves. Nobody would see a failure.

Why this matters beyond the five: `{{.ComponentID}}` resolves to the content_components ROW id on both live render paths, so every instance of a component takes the same value. Measured live 2026-08-22: 18 pages carry a repeated {{.ComponentID}} component (27 redundant placements; 13 pages x2, three x3, one x4, one x6, all generic-text-block), and apis.uk/index.html serves six identical `<section id="8d81e665-3ee0-443d-a873-690268c15fbb">`, verified by live fetch and re-confirmed cache-busted. A further 11 placements serve `<section id="">` because the section editor binds ComponentID at all. Single-instance pages were read as controls and show 1 id, 0 duplicates, so the reading could have come out otherwise.

There is a second, worse defect in the same regex that this closes at the same time. A template mixing literal ids AND {{.ComponentID}} converts 'successfully' today: the literals are prefixed and the templated id is silently ignored. GateConvertedTemplate cannot catch the residue, because it renders with only InstanceID bound, so the surviving {{.ComponentID}} resolves through missingkey=zero to "" and is stripped — and DetectInstanceCollisions cannot report it, because reElementID requires one or more NON-BRACE characters and so cannot match an empty id. Two instances would read CLEAN at the gate while serving colliding empty ids: a half-conversion with the warning light removed, which is precisely what this file's stated failure direction exists to prevent. Measured 2026-08-22: 0 active templates are currently in that mixed state (control: 87 active templates carry a literal id at all), so the guard refuses nothing today and is there for the arrival that half-learns the convention.

Scope claim, stated so it can be checked rather than taken on trust: this is NOT architecture-scope under the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 section 1. It changes no shared mechanism's guarantee. {{.InstanceID}}'s guarantee is unchanged and already council-approved (CLC-014); the conversion route is the one RFC_034 ruled on and under which 124 rows have already converted, so the five are late arrivals to an existing programme. ComponentID's own writers are NOT touched by this change and will be deleted only in a later commit, after its consumer count is measured zero — guarantee-neutral by construction. No opt-in field is proposed for this step and the 2026-08-02 section 2 ruling is argued not to bite: the change confers no new authority (no power to refuse, delete or re-type that did not exist), it only stops a REFUSAL that was wrong. The one genuinely new refusal — the surviving-placeholder guard — makes the function stricter in the direction the file already declares, and refuses nothing in the current corpus.

Other consumers of the seam, named and told rather than merely measured (2026-07-29 section 3): pass 0 also runs inside both existing birth guards, because ScopeToolBirthTemplate calls this same function — so create_tool_component and deploy_tool_to_site gain the ability to convert a newborn template that spells the old name, which they previously refused as 'no literal element ids'. That is a strict improvement in the same direction, and it is the reason this is a defect fix rather than a widening of remit. The webdesign_tool_rebuilds and bugfix_311_component_keys lanes touch the same birth path and are named in the lane docs.

plan.summary: The deterministic instance-scope converter REFUSES the five templates whose only id is written as the retired {{.ComponentID}} placeholder, because its declared-id regex excludes braces and so reports "template declares no literal element ids" on a template that plainly declares one. Filing those five through the proven conversion pipeline today would produce five polite no-op completions and a census that never moves. This adds pass 0 — an id attribute whose whole value is {{.ComponentID}} becomes {{.InstanceID}} — plus a completeness refusal for the placeholder anywhere pass 0 cannot safely rewrite, which closes a half-state the acceptance gate provably cannot see. It converts no template, touches no render path, and changes no live behaviour by itself: it makes the owner's RFC_032 ruling executable.

edits.rationale: Add pass 0: an id attribute whose whole value is the retired {{.ComponentID}} placeholder becomes {{.InstanceID}}. It must run BEFORE the declared-id harvest, because that harvest cannot see a templated id. The harvest then reads the swapped text rather than the input, so the swapped wrapper is neither double-prefixed nor renamed by the later passes (the harvest cannot see {{.InstanceID}} either, for the same brace-excluding reason). The refusal condition becomes len(seen)==0 AND TemplatedIDSwaps==0, so a wrapper-only template proceeds. The wrapper takes the BARE token, not the {{.InstanceID}}- prefix, because this id IS the instance identity rather than an id scoped within it; the prefix form would render 'c-faq-' with a trailing hyphen and nothing after it.

Completeness refusal for the half-state the gate cannot see. Pass 0 rewrites the placeholder only where it is an id attribute's whole value; a reference anywhere else (a data-* value, a #selector, a script literal) cannot be swapped mechanically and would render EMPTY on every instance, invisibly to both GateConvertedTemplate and DetectInstanceCollisions. Refusing the whole component matches this file's declared failure direction: a refused component is exactly as broken as it was yesterday, a half-converted one is broken in a new way with the warning light removed.

Two package-level regexes and one report field. reComponentIDInIDAttr is deliberately tolerant of Go template whitespace and trim markers ({{- .ComponentID -}}) because the corpus is LLM-written and a spelling this missed would be silently left behind rather than loudly refused. reComponentIDAnywhere backs the completeness refusal. TemplatedIDSwaps is reported separately from IDAttrsRenamed because it is a different act — those are literal ids gaining a namespace, this is one convention being replaced by the one that works.

Six tests, each RUN AGAINST THE UNPATCHED CONVERTER FIRST and observed to fail for the stated reason — pass 0's regex was mutated to be unmatchable and all six failed, the wrapper-only case with exactly the pre-change message 'template declares no literal element ids'. The mutation was aimed at pass 0 specifically rather than at the function as a whole, because a guard in series can absorb a mutation and pass for the wrong reason. Coverage: the wrapper-only shape converts and gates; the gate REFUSES the unconverted template first, as a control, so its later pass is evidence rather than an accept-everything result; two rendered instances do not collide, asserted by requiring BOTH tokens to be present (a page of two EMPTY ids would also report no duplicate non-empty ids, so the absence alone is not evidence) plus a control that the detector DOES report the unconverted two-instance page; a mixed literal+templated template converts both; a placeholder outside an id attribute refuses in three positions; the swap is not re-runnable; and TemplateNeedsInstanceID still does not fire on the retired placeholder, the pre-existing contract most at risk from this change.

grounded_in: component_instance_conversion.go:102-113 — the declared-id harvest: regexp.MustCompile(`\sid="([^"{}]+)"`) and the single-quote twin. The [^"{}] class excludes braces, which is why a templated id never enters `seen`.

component_instance_conversion.go:111 — `if len(seen) == 0 { rep.RefusedReason = "template declares no literal element ids — nothing to namespace"; return tpl, rep, false }` — the refusal that fires on the five templates.
component_instance_scope.go:215 — reElementID requires one or more characters excluding braces, so DetectInstanceCollisions cannot match id="" and cannot report the mixed-template half-state.

call_agent.go:1172 — executeGoTemplate sets Option("missingkey=zero"); component_library.go:1170 strips the resulting <no value>. Together these turn a surviving placeholder into an empty id rather than a visible error.

Live census 2026-08-22: 5 active templates match html_template LIKE '%ComponentID%'; control in the same statement, 125 match '%InstanceID%' (a healthy zero from a broken LIKE is indistinguishable from success).

Live census 2026-08-22: 18 pages carry a repeated {{.ComponentID}} component, 27 redundant placements. Controlled: the same query shape returns 29 for any component repeated on a page and the population is 130 getElementById placements, so the figure is not an artefact of a broken predicate.

Live artefact 2026-08-22, HTTP 200, cache-busted: apis.uk/index.html serves six <section id="8d81e665-3ee0-443d-a873-690268c15fbb">. Negative controls ai-agent-orchestration.com/privacy.html and dartsonline.com/privacy.html (DB says ONE instance each) serve 1 id and 0 duplicates.

Live census 2026-08-22: 0 active templates mix a literal id with {{.ComponentID}}; control, 87 active templates carry a literal id at all — so the new completeness guard refuses nothing in the current corpus.

Live census 2026-08-22: 0 of 270 placements of the five components carry the assemble-path id shape component_<fn>_<n>; the regex was proved against a synthetic positive (1 match) before the zero was believed, then widened case-insensitively. This is why RFC_032 section 2's table is corrected in the same round.

Mutation proof, this session: pass 0's regex replaced with an unmatchable literal; all six new tests FAILED, the wrapper-only case with the exact pre-change refusal reason; source restored from backup and verified (0 occurrences of the mutant literal) and the suite re-run green, including the pre-existing Instance/Scope/Conversion/Binding tests.
architecture_review/RFC_032 section 8 — the owner ruling of 2026-08-22 this implements, with the blast-radius measurement section 4 asked for and a dated correction to the RFC's own section 2 table.
plan.risks:
What a reviewer should check, in order.

1) DOUBLE-PREFIXING. Pass 0 writes {{.InstanceID}} and the later literal-id passes must not then treat that as a declared id. They cannot: the harvest's [^"{}] class excludes braces, which is the same property that caused the original defect. The harvest reads `swapped` rather than `tpl` precisely so this holds; TestConvertTemplateToInstanceScope_MixedLiteralAndTemplatedID pins it by asserting the wrapper stays id="{{.InstanceID}}" while the literals become id="{{.InstanceID}}-amount".

2) BARE TOKEN vs PREFIX. The wrapper takes the bare token, not the {{.InstanceID}}- prefix, because this id IS the instance identity. If a reviewer disagrees, the failure mode is visible: the prefix form renders 'c-faq-' with a trailing hyphen and nothing after it, and a test asserts against that.

3) THE NEW REFUSAL'S BLAST RADIUS. reComponentIDAnywhere refuses a component when the placeholder survives outside an id attribute. Measured 2026-08-22: 0 active templates are in that state (control: 87 carry a literal id at all), so it refuses nothing today. If that census is stale by the time this lands, re-run it — a template arriving in that shape now fails its conversion item loudly instead of converting half-way, which is the intended direction but is a behaviour change for that row.

4) BOTH BIRTH GUARDS INHERIT THIS. ScopeToolBirthTemplate calls the same function, so create_tool_component and deploy_tool_to_site can now convert a newborn template spelling the old name where they previously refused it. Strictly better, and the reason this is a defect fix rather than a widening of remit — but it is a live behaviour change on two armed guards and should be read as one.

5) WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, so it is not credited with it: it does not convert the five templates, does not delete ComponentID's two bindings or the dead ReplaceAll in assemble_from_library, and does not re-render anything. The 18 pages serving duplicate section ids are still serving them after this commit ships.

6) TEST HONESTY. All six tests were mutation-proven — pass 0's regex made unmatchable, all six failed, the wrapper-only case with the exact pre-change refusal reason, source then restored and verified. The gate test carries a control that the gate REFUSES the unconverted template, and the collision test carries a control that the detector DOES report the unconverted two-instance page, because an empty-id page would also produce 'no duplicate non-empty ids'.
